stage_a.note: Founders maintain bright smiles and high energy throughout the entire presentation, conveying strong enthusiasm.
Founders speak with pronounced excitement about the product's effect and features, using animated gestures.
Founders are highly approachable and friendly, addressing the panel with warm smiles and inviting tone.

venture.description: A styling tool that easily applies adhesive gems and crystals to hair.
venture.note: The product is presented as a beauty and styling tool with fashion applications.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founders pitch Blinger, a hair styling tool that easily applies adhesive gems, seeking 200k for 5 percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara jokes that all the sharks are ready to bling it on.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks what the difference is between the two versions of the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie explains the main difference is the inclusion of Swarovski crystals in the women's version.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin puts on a wig and says he likes the look.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks how much the products cost.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie states the women's version is 49 dollars and the girl's version is 29.99.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if she can try the product on Kevin's wig.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori successfully applies a gem to Kevin's wig.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that he is shining bright.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark jokes that putting the gems on his fingers makes him invisible.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks how long they have been selling the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie explains it took four years and five engineering firms to get a working prototype.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara jokes that being a single mom is no excuse not to succeed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie says she was in massive debt by the time the fifth engineer designed the tool.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks exactly how much debt she was in.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie reveals she had put in 1.7 million dollars and was maxed out on debt.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie describes gathering her kids to suggest selling their house to fund the tooling.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks to confirm if she actually sold her house.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie confirms selling the house, going to the Dallas Toy Fair, and getting rumored as toy of the year.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks what happened after the toy fair.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie says she pitched to two toy companies, got offers, and took a licensing deal.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if the toy companies gave her a royalty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie confirms she received a 5 percent royalty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie adds that the companies did over 20 million dollars wholesale in 2019.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert expresses amazement at the sales figure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie says the success absolutely changed their lives.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks what happened next in their business journey.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie explains that COVID caused sales and her income to drop significantly.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks if she expected the royalties to continue coming in.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie says she expected them to continue but they dropped sharply in 2021.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie mentions that by summer 2022 Serena Williams was wearing Swarovski crystals in her hair.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie explains that despite rising demand, illegal infringers flooded the internet with knockoffs.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara acknowledges that the product was knocked off.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie confirms they were totally knocked off by competitors.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks if the product category grew even though her specific sales did not.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie explains she had retained the women's market as part of her licensing deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks to clarify if she retained the rights but hadn't started selling the product yet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie confirms she had not activated those rights yet.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks why the toy company returned the rights to her.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if she broke the agreement to get the rights back.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie clarifies that the toy company willingly gave the rights back to her.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks to confirm if she now owns 100 percent of both product lines.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie confirms she owns the rights moving forward.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks if she is free and clear and currently making sales.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark prompts her to explain the company's current status.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie states they currently have 1.64 million dollars in sales.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks if that sales figure is for the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie confirms it is and adds that they are profitable.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks exactly how profitable the company is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie says they project to finish the year with 1.5 million dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks to clarify if that 1.5 million figure represents sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie corrects herself, stating that is profit and sales should end at 4.2 million.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert expresses surprise at the projected jump from 1.7 to 4.2 million in sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie lists upcoming deals with CVS and QVC to support her projection.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks where the cash went if they have such high margins.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie explains that all the cash is tied up in 2.5 million dollars worth of inventory.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark expresses surprise at the large amount of inventory.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks what she plans to do with the 200k she is asking for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie admits she lacks business experience and needs help running the operations.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks if she has a Chief Financial Officer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie says they do not have a CFO and desperately need a bookkeeper.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks how they keep their books and track profitability without a bookkeeper.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie admits it is a problem and they are struggling to put out operational fires.

turns.speaker: PANEL
turns.summary: The panel laughs at Angie's analogy about putting out fires.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin exits, stating her operations are too messy for an investor right now.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark exits, saying she needs an operator and he does not want to be CEO.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara offers 200k for 25 percent of the company.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark advises Angie to accept Barbara's offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara explains she wants to add a contingency to her offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara revises her offer to 200k for 25 percent, contingent on Angie coming to New York for mentoring.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert exits, agreeing that Angie is a dreamer who needs an operator like Barbara.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori exits, agreeing that Barbara's offer is the right fit for the business.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks Angie what she wants to do regarding the offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie expresses hesitation, feeling that giving up 25 percent is too high.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin advises her not to take the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie asks Barbara if she would also be willing to fund purchase orders.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara repeats the question, noting that funding is one of their issues.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks to confirm if Angie will accept the deal if POs are funded.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie counters with an offer of 20 percent equity.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara refuses 20 percent but agrees to fund purchase orders while keeping equity at 25 percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark encourages Angie to take the revised offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Angie accepts Barbara's revised offer.

turns.speaker: PANEL
turns.summary: The founders and sharks celebrate the successful deal.
